statement: Let n=34; map digits 0,1,2,3 to 1,i,-1,-i; take A=2202202000022020222202000220200020 and B=1133303133112311101113211331303331; define (c_r X)_j=X_{j-r} and (d_k X)_j=X_{j k^{-1}} on Z_34; and let Gamma_34(A,B) be exactly the set of s^e(alpha c_r d_k(A^epsilon), beta c_t d_k(B^epsilon)) with alpha,beta in {1,i,-1,-i}, r,t in Z_34, k in Z_34^times, and epsilon,e in {0,1}. Then Gamma_34(A,B) contains no ordered pair whose four Gray rows all satisfy x_j=x_{-j} for every j in Z_34. This is only a conclusion about the displayed frozen Gamma_34, not about any larger qLP equivalence relation or other length-34 qLPs.
contribution: This completely answers the frozen finite-orbit question negatively. A paper-checkable 17-axis obstruction proves that every permitted pair retains a transform of A whose two Gray rows cannot both be reversible. An exact census independently reconstructs all 1,183,744 parameter tuples, finds 1,183,744 distinct ordered images, fixes a canonical orbit digest, and supplies and separately recomputes one deterministic reflection-failure witness for every image. The nearest primary source establishes only failure in the printed orientation; no priority claim is made beyond this explicitly named orbit.
